question: Is purity or impurity a property of the knower or of the object?
premises: Purity and impurity arise from experiencing unity or non-unity with consciousness.
This makes them primarily properties of the knower.
Even if treated as properties of objects, they depend on a limiting measure.
inference: Purity and impurity belong to the knower's relation to consciousness, and any object-based account still depends on that relation.
uncertainties: mātrā may refer to a limiting measure, standpoint, or cognitive frame.
plain_english: This distinction is really a property of the knower, arising from the experience of unity or non-unity with consciousness. Even if one treats it as a property of objects, it still depends on a limiting standpoint.
